title: Computer Science pseudocode
subject: Computer Science
syllabus: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science (9618)
description: Official Cambridge pseudocode: model answers from 9618 mark schemes plus constructs from the Pseudocode Guide.

items.prompt: Declare an INTEGER variable Counter, a REAL variable TotalToPay, a BOOLEAN variable GameOver, and constants HourlyRate (6.50) and DefaultText ("N/A").
items.answer:
DECLARE Counter : INTEGER
DECLARE TotalToPay : REAL
DECLARE GameOver : BOOLEAN
CONSTANT HourlyRate = 6.50
CONSTANT DefaultText = "N/A"
items.notes: Example declarations from the guide (sections 2.4 and 2.5) combined. Constants take a literal value only.

items.prompt: Output who is champion, comparing ChallengerScore with ChampionScore and with HighestScore (nested IF with ELSE).
items.answer:
IF ChallengerScore > ChampionScore THEN
    IF ChallengerScore > HighestScore THEN
        OUTPUT ChallengerName, " is champion and highest scorer"
    ELSE
        OUTPUT ChallengerName, " is the new champion"
    ENDIF
ELSE
    OUTPUT ChampionName, " is still the champion"
    IF ChampionScore > HighestScore THEN
        OUTPUT ChampionName, " is also the highest scorer"
    ENDIF
ENDIF
items.notes: Every IF needs its own ENDIF; the inner IF is indented one level.

items.prompt: Input a character Move and use a CASE statement to change Position by -10 for 'W', +10 for 'S', -1 for 'A' and +1 for 'D'; any other value calls procedure Beep.
items.answer:
INPUT Move
CASE OF Move
    'W' : Position <- Position - 10
    'S' : Position <- Position + 10
    'A' : Position <- Position - 1
    'D' : Position <- Position + 1
    OTHERWISE : CALL Beep
ENDCASE
items.notes: Char literals use single quotes. OTHERWISE must be the last case. The guide uses a true minus sign; ASCII hyphen used here.

items.prompt: Using the 2D array Amount, output the total of each row (10 columns, MaxRow rows) and then the grand total.
items.answer:
Total <- 0
FOR Row <- 1 TO MaxRow
    RowTotal <- 0
    FOR Column <- 1 TO 10
        RowTotal <- RowTotal + Amount[Row, Column]
    NEXT Column
    OUTPUT "Total for Row ", Row, " is ", RowTotal
    Total <- Total + RowTotal
NEXT Row
OUTPUT "The grand total is ", Total
items.notes: Repeat the loop identifier after NEXT, especially for nested loops.

items.prompt: Repeatedly ask for a password until the user enters "Secret".
items.answer:
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "Please enter the password"
    INPUT Password
UNTIL Password = "Secret"
items.notes: A post-condition loop: the body always runs at least once and the loop ends when the condition is TRUE.

items.prompt: Reduce Number by 9 repeatedly while it is greater than 9.
items.answer:
WHILE Number > 9
    Number <- Number - 9
ENDWHILE
items.notes: A pre-condition loop: the condition is tested before each pass, so the body may not run at all.

items.prompt: Write pseudocode that inputs 100 integers, one at a time, and outputs the total of the positive values only.
items.answer:
DECLARE Count, Total, NextNumber : INTEGER
Total <- 0
FOR Count <- 1 TO 100
    OUTPUT "Input an integer value"
    INPUT NextNumber
    IF NextNumber > 0 THEN
        Total <- Total + NextNumber
    ENDIF
NEXT Count
OUTPUT Total
items.notes: Marks: declarations, initialise Total, count-controlled loop of 100, input, test for positive, accumulate, output after the loop.

items.prompt: Write pseudocode for a game: generate a random integer from 1 to 100, repeatedly ask for a guess and say whether it was too high or too low, until the guess is correct.
items.answer:
DECLARE GeneratedValue : INTEGER
DECLARE Guess : INTEGER
GeneratedValue <- INT(RAND(100)) + 1
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "Enter a guess between 1 and 100: "
    INPUT Guess
    IF Guess > GeneratedValue THEN
        OUTPUT "Guess was too high"
    ENDIF
    IF Guess < GeneratedValue THEN
        OUTPUT "Guess was too low"
    ENDIF
UNTIL Guess = GeneratedValue
OUTPUT "Number guessed correctly"
items.notes: RAND(100) gives a real in the range 0 to 100 (not inclusive), so INT(RAND(100)) + 1 gives 1 to 100.

items.prompt: Write a procedure Count() that inputs integers until 99 is entered, then outputs how many were odd and how many were even.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE Count()
    DECLARE COdd, CEven, ThisNum : INTEGER
    COdd <- 0
    CEven <- 0
    INPUT ThisNum
    WHILE ThisNum <> 99
        IF ThisNum MOD 2 = 1 THEN
            COdd <- COdd + 1
        ELSE
            CEven <- CEven + 1
        ENDIF
        INPUT ThisNum
    ENDWHILE
    OUTPUT "Count of odd and even numbers: ", COdd, CEven
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Input before the loop and again at the end of the loop body, so 99 itself is not counted.

items.prompt: Declare a 1D array StudentNames of 30 STRING elements, then use a loop to set every element to the empty string.
items.answer:
DECLARE StudentNames : ARRAY[1:30] OF STRING
FOR Index <- 1 TO 30
    StudentNames[Index] <- ""
NEXT Index
items.notes: Declaration from 3.1 followed by the loop from 3.2; a group of elements is never assigned in one statement.

items.prompt: Define a record type StudentRecord holding LastName, FirstName (STRING), DateOfBirth (DATE), YearGroup (INTEGER) and FormGroup (CHAR).
items.answer:
TYPE StudentRecord
    DECLARE LastName : STRING
    DECLARE FirstName : STRING
    DECLARE DateOfBirth : DATE
    DECLARE YearGroup : INTEGER
    DECLARE FormGroup : CHAR
ENDTYPE

items.prompt: Write a function GetNum(ThisString, ThisChar) that returns the number of times ThisChar appears in ThisString.
items.answer:
FUNCTION GetNum(ThisString : STRING, ThisChar : CHAR) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Index, Count : INTEGER
    Count <- 0
    FOR Index <- 1 TO LENGTH(ThisString)
        IF MID(ThisString, Index, 1) = ThisChar THEN
            Count <- Count + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
    RETURN Count
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The heading in the mark scheme wraps over two lines (RETURNS INTEGER). Marks: heading/end, local integers, loop over LENGTH, MID comparison, increment, RETURN after loop.

items.prompt: Write a function MakeString(Count, AChar) that returns a string of Count copies of AChar, or "ERROR" if Count is less than 1.
items.answer:
FUNCTION MakeString(Count : INTEGER, AChar : CHAR) RETURNS STRING
    DECLARE MyString : STRING
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    IF Count < 1 THEN
        MyString <- "ERROR"
    ELSE
        MyString <- ""
        FOR Index <- 1 TO Count
            MyString <- MyString & AChar
        NEXT Index
    ENDIF
    RETURN MyString
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: String concatenation uses &. Declaration layout tidied; logic unchanged.

items.prompt: Write a function Parity(BitString) that counts the '1' characters in a bit string and returns the string with '1' appended if the count is odd, otherwise '0'.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Parity(BitString : STRING) RETURNS STRING
    DECLARE Index, Count : INTEGER
    Count <- 0
    FOR Index <- 1 TO LENGTH(BitString)
        IF MID(BitString, Index, 1) = '1' THEN
            Count <- Count + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
    IF Count MOD 2 = 1 THEN
        BitString <- BitString & '1'
    ELSE
        BitString <- BitString & '0'
    ENDIF
    RETURN BitString
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Marks: count the 1s in a loop, test odd/even with MOD, append the parity bit, return the string.

items.term: Unpack a text line with BYREF parameters
items.prompt: Write a procedure UnPack(TLine, SID, SDesc, SCost) that splits a line: SID is the first 5 characters, SDesc the next 32 characters, SCost everything after character 37. SID, SDesc and SCost are passed by reference.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE UnPack(BYVAL TLine : STRING, BYREF SID, SDesc, SCost : STRING)
    SID <- LEFT(TLine, 5)
    SDesc <- MID(TLine, 6, 32)
    SCost <- RIGHT(TLine, LENGTH(TLine) - 37)
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: The heading wraps over two lines in the mark scheme. BYVAL/BYREF apply to the parameters that follow them. The mark scheme uses an en dash before 37; ASCII hyphen used here.

items.prompt: Write a function DeleteComment(Line) that returns Line with any comment (from the first "//" onwards) removed.
items.answer:
FUNCTION DeleteComment(Line : STRING) RETURNS STRING
    DECLARE NewLine, TwoChars : STRING
    DECLARE Count, TrimTo : INTEGER
    CONSTANT Comment = "//"
    NewLine <- Line
    TrimTo <- 0
    Count <- 1
    WHILE Count < LENGTH(Line) AND TrimTo = 0
        TwoChars <- MID(Line, Count, 2)
        IF TwoChars = Comment THEN
            TrimTo <- Count
        ENDIF
        Count <- Count + 1
    ENDWHILE
    IF TrimTo <> 0 THEN
        NewLine <- LEFT(Line, TrimTo - 1)
    ENDIF
    RETURN NewLine
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The model answer's short // comment was dropped. Marks: constant for the comment marker, loop that extracts two characters at a time, record the trim position, LEFT to trim, return.

items.term: Average of selected values in a 2D array
items.prompt: Sample is a 2D array [1:6, 1:128] of INTEGER. For each of the 128 samples, find the average (whole number) of the values greater than 10 across the 6 users and store it in Result.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE Mix()
    DECLARE Count, Total, ThisNum : INTEGER
    DECLARE ThisUser, ThisSample : INTEGER
    FOR ThisSample <- 1 TO 128
        Count <- 0
        Total <- 0
        FOR ThisUser <- 1 TO 6
            IF Sample[ThisUser, ThisSample] > 10 THEN
                Count <- Count + 1
                Total <- Total + Sample[ThisUser, ThisSample]
            ENDIF
        NEXT ThisUser
        Result[ThisSample] <- INT(Total / Count)
    NEXT ThisSample
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Fixed a missing comma in the mark scheme's DECLARE line (Total ThisNum). Marks: nested loops, reset Count and Total for each sample, conditional accumulation, INT of the average.

items.prompt: Write a procedure DefaultSquare() that calls procedure Square with 100, and a procedure Square(Size) that moves forward Size and turns 90 degrees four times.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE DefaultSquare()
    CALL Square(100)
ENDPROCEDURE
PROCEDURE Square(Size : INTEGER)
    FOR Side <- 1 TO 4
        CALL MoveForward(Size)
        CALL Turn(90)
    NEXT Side
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Procedures are invoked with CALL, which is a complete statement. Blank lines in the guide's layout were dropped.

items.prompt: Write a function Max(Number1, Number2) that returns the larger of two integers.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Max(Number1 : INTEGER, Number2 : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Number1 > Number2 THEN
        RETURN Number1
    ELSE
        RETURN Number2
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: A function's definition states the type returned. Functions are called inside expressions, never with CALL.

items.prompt: Write a procedure SWAP that exchanges the values of two integers passed by reference.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE SWAP(BYREF X : INTEGER, Y : INTEGER)
    Temp <- X
    X <- Y
    Y <- Temp
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: BYREF need not be repeated for parameters passed by the same method.

items.prompt: Write a function IsRA(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3) that takes the coordinates of a triangle's corners and returns TRUE if it is right-angled, using the squares of the side lengths.
items.answer:
FUNCTION IsRA(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3 : INTEGER) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    DECLARE Len1, Len2, Len3 : INTEGER
    Len1 <- (x1 - x2) ^ 2 + (y1 - y2) ^ 2
    Len2 <- (x1 - x3) ^ 2 + (y1 - y3) ^ 2
    Len3 <- (x2 - x3) ^ 2 + (y2 - y3) ^ 2
    IF (Len1 = Len2 + Len3) OR (Len2 = Len1 + Len3) OR (Len3 = Len1 + Len2) THEN
        RETURN TRUE
    ELSE
        RETURN FALSE
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The mark scheme splits the IF condition over three lines with the continuation marker __; joined onto one line here. Heading also wrapped in the mark scheme.

items.prompt: Write a function Status(Actual, Min, Max) returning 'R' if Actual is more than 2 outside the range Min to Max, 'A' if it is more than 2 inside the range, otherwise 'C'.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Status(Actual, Min, Max : INTEGER) RETURNS CHAR
    DECLARE Result : CHAR
    CONSTANT Accept = 'A'
    CONSTANT Reject = 'R'
    CONSTANT ReCheck = 'C'
    Result <- ReCheck
    IF Actual > Max + 2 OR Actual < Min - 2 THEN
        Result <- Reject
    ENDIF
    IF Actual < Max - 2 AND Actual > Min + 2 THEN
        Result <- Accept
    ENDIF
    RETURN Result
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Keyword capitalised (the mark scheme has 'Function') and en dash replaced with a hyphen; two short // comments dropped. A default result is set first, then overridden by each test.

items.term: Find the number whose factorial is given (function)
items.prompt: Write a function FindBaseNumber(ThisValue) that returns the integer Num such that Num factorial equals ThisValue, or -1 if there is no such number.
items.answer:
FUNCTION FindBaseNumber(ThisValue : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Num, Try : INTEGER
    Try <- 1
    FOR Num <- 1 TO ThisValue
        Try <- Try * Num
        IF Try = ThisValue THEN
            RETURN Num
        ENDIF
    NEXT Num
    RETURN -1
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Second of the two example solutions (loop with early RETURN). Heading wrapped over two lines in the mark scheme.

items.prompt: Write a function Generate(Number) that adds up the digits of Number, takes the total MOD 10 as a check digit, appends it to the number and returns the new number.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Generate(Number : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Total, Index, CheckDigit : INTEGER
    DECLARE NumString : STRING
    Total <- 0
    NumString <- NUM_TO_STR(Number)
    FOR Index <- 1 TO LENGTH(NumString)
        Total <- Total + STR_TO_NUM(MID(NumString, Index, 1))
    NEXT Index
    CheckDigit <- Total MOD 10
    Number <- Number * 10 + CheckDigit
    RETURN Number
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: First example solution. The alternative inline comments were dropped. Appending the check digit is done arithmetically (x10 + digit).

items.term: Date of the third Sunday in March (function)
items.prompt: Write a function AdjustClock(ThisYear) that returns the day number in March of the third Sunday, using SETDATE() and DAYINDEX() (Sunday has index 1).
items.answer:
FUNCTION AdjustClock(ThisYear : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE ThisDayNumber, SundayCount : INTEGER
    DECLARE ThisDate : DATE
    ThisDayNumber <- 0
    SundayCount <- 0
    REPEAT
        ThisDayNumber <- ThisDayNumber + 1
        ThisDate <- SETDATE(ThisDayNumber, 3, ThisYear)
        IF DAYINDEX(ThisDate) = 1 THEN
            SundayCount <- SundayCount + 1
        ENDIF
    UNTIL SundayCount = 3
    RETURN ThisDayNumber
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: First example solution (loop through the days counting Sundays). SETDATE and DAYINDEX are provided date functions.

items.prompt: Write a function RollDice(NoOfTimes) that simulates rolling a six-sided die NoOfTimes, outputs each roll, and returns the average roll.
items.answer:
FUNCTION RollDice(NoOfTimes : INTEGER) RETURNS REAL
    DECLARE RollValue : INTEGER
    DECLARE Average : REAL
    DECLARE Count : INTEGER
    DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
    Sum <- 0
    FOR Count <- 1 TO NoOfTimes
        RollValue <- INT(RAND(6)) + 1
        OUTPUT RollValue
        Sum <- Sum + RollValue
    NEXT Count
    Average <- Sum / NoOfTimes
    RETURN Average
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Marks: heading with REAL return, random 1 to 6 with INT(RAND(6)) + 1, loop NoOfTimes, output, running sum, average and RETURN.

items.prompt: Loyalty is a 2D array [1:1000, 1:2] holding customer ID and points, with unused rows holding ID 99999 at the end. Write a function FindCustomer(CustomerID) returning the customer's points, or -1 if the ID is out of range (10001 to 11000) or not found.
items.answer:
FUNCTION FindCustomer(CustomerID : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    IF CustomerID < 10001 OR CustomerID > 11000 THEN
        RETURN -1
    ENDIF
    FOR Index <- 1 TO 1000
        IF Loyalty[Index, 1] = CustomerID THEN
            RETURN Loyalty[Index, 2]
        ENDIF
        IF Loyalty[Index, 1] = 99999 THEN
            RETURN -1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: One of several example solutions (linear search with early RETURN). The heading is wrapped over two lines in the mark scheme; the short // comment was dropped.

items.term: Binary search of a sorted 2D array (function)
items.prompt: Loyalty is sorted by customer ID. Write a function FindCustomer(CustomerID) using a binary search that returns the customer's points (column 2), or -1 if the ID is out of range (10001 to 11000) or not found.
items.answer:
FUNCTION FindCustomer(CustomerID : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Start : INTEGER
    DECLARE End : INTEGER
    DECLARE Mid : INTEGER
    IF CustomerID < 10001 OR CustomerID > 11000 THEN
        RETURN -1
    ENDIF
    Start <- 1
    End <- 1000
    WHILE Start <= End
        Mid <- (Start + End) DIV 2
        IF Loyalty[Mid, 1] = CustomerID THEN
            RETURN Loyalty[Mid, 2]
        ELSE
            IF Loyalty[Mid, 1] > CustomerID THEN
                End <- Mid - 1
            ELSE
                Start <- Mid + 1
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN -1
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The mark scheme writes the middle branch as 'ELSE IF' with a single ENDIF; written here as an ELSE containing a nested IF so every IF has its own ENDIF. Short // comment dropped.

items.term: Binary search of a sorted array (program)
items.prompt: Names is a sorted array [1:100000] of STRING. Write pseudocode that asks for a name and uses a binary search (flags Found and NotInList, pointers TopOfList, EndOfList and CurrentItem) to look for it.
items.answer:
TopOfList <- 1
EndOfList <- 100000
OUTPUT "Which name do you wish to find? "
INPUT ToFind
Found <- FALSE
NotInList <- FALSE
WHILE Found = FALSE AND NotInList = FALSE
    CurrentItem <- (TopOfList + EndOfList) DIV 2
    IF ToFind = Names[CurrentItem] THEN
        Found <- TRUE
    ELSE
        IF TopOfList >= EndOfList THEN
            NotInList <- TRUE
        ELSE
            IF ToFind > Names[CurrentItem] THEN
                TopOfList <- CurrentItem + 1
            ELSE
                EndOfList <- CurrentItem - 1
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
items.notes: Gap-fill question; this is the whole search loop. The seven DECLARE lines at the top and the final IF that outputs the result are omitted. The mark scheme accepts Names[CurrentItem] = ToFind as well.

items.prompt: Names is a sorted array with indices 0 to 99. Write pseudocode that inputs a Target name, uses a binary search, and outputs the location where it was found or that it does not exist.
items.answer:
Lower <- 0
Upper <- 99
Mid <- 0
Exit <- FALSE
OUTPUT "Enter the name to be found "
INPUT Target
REPEAT
    IF Upper < Lower THEN
        OUTPUT Target, " does not exist"
        Exit <- TRUE
    ENDIF
    Mid <- Lower + (Upper - Lower + 1) DIV 2
    IF Names[Mid] < Target THEN
        Lower <- Mid + 1
    ENDIF
    IF Names[Mid] > Target THEN
        Upper <- Mid - 1
    ENDIF
    IF Names[Mid] = Target THEN
        OUTPUT Target, " was found at location ", Mid
        Exit <- TRUE
    ENDIF
UNTIL Exit
items.notes: The mark scheme also accepts UNTIL Exit = TRUE. En dash replaced with a hyphen.

items.term: Linear search of a sorted array (procedure)
items.prompt: ErrCode[1:500] is sorted in ascending order with the matching messages in ErrText. Write a procedure OutputError(LineNum, ErrNum) that searches for ErrNum and outputs its message and the line number, or 'Unknown error' with the line number if it is not present.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE OutputError(LineNum, ErrNum : INTEGER)
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    Index <- 0
    REPEAT
        Index <- Index + 1
    UNTIL ErrCode[Index] >= ErrNum OR Index = 500
    IF ErrCode[Index] = ErrNum THEN
        OUTPUT ErrText[Index], " on line ", LineNum
    ELSE
        OUTPUT "Unknown error on line ", LineNum
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Stops as soon as the element is found or passes where it would be (sorted data). The mark scheme misspells the end keyword as ENDPROCEURE; corrected. // comments dropped.

items.term: Bubble sort with a flag (parallel arrays)
items.prompt: Write a procedure SortArrays() that sorts ErrCode[1:500] into ascending order using a bubble sort with a NoSwaps flag, keeping the parallel array ErrText in step.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE SortArrays()
    DECLARE TempInt, J, Boundary : INTEGER
    DECLARE TempStr : STRING
    DECLARE NoSwaps : BOOLEAN
    Boundary <- 499
    REPEAT
        NoSwaps <- TRUE
        FOR J <- 1 TO Boundary
            IF ErrCode[J] > ErrCode[J + 1] THEN
                TempInt <- ErrCode[J]
                ErrCode[J] <- ErrCode[J + 1]
                ErrCode[J + 1] <- TempInt
                TempStr <- ErrText[J]
                ErrText[J] <- ErrText[J + 1]
                ErrText[J + 1] <- TempStr
                NoSwaps <- FALSE
            ENDIF
        NEXT J
        Boundary <- Boundary - 1
    UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Marks: flag reset each pass, inner loop to a shrinking boundary, compare neighbours, swap using a temporary (both arrays), set the flag, stop when no swaps. // comments dropped.

items.prompt: Reading is a 2D array [1:2000, 1:2] holding a sensor value (column 1) and an ID (column 2). Write a procedure Sort() that sorts the rows into ascending order of sensor value using a bubble sort with a NoSwaps flag.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE Sort()
    DECLARE Temp, J, Boundary : INTEGER
    DECLARE NoSwaps : BOOLEAN
    Boundary <- 1999
    REPEAT
        NoSwaps <- TRUE
        FOR J <- 1 TO Boundary
            IF Reading[J, 1] > Reading[J + 1, 1] THEN
                Temp <- Reading[J, 1]
                Reading[J, 1] <- Reading[J + 1, 1]
                Reading[J + 1, 1] <- Temp
                Temp <- Reading[J, 2]
                Reading[J, 2] <- Reading[J + 1, 2]
                Reading[J + 1, 2] <- Temp
                NoSwaps <- FALSE
            ENDIF
        NEXT J
        Boundary <- Boundary - 1
    UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Both columns of the row are swapped using the same temporary. // comments dropped.

items.prompt: Write pseudocode that sorts the array DataArray[1:1000] into ascending order using an insertion sort.
items.answer:
FOR Index <- 2 TO 1000
    Value <- DataArray[Index]
    Position <- Index - 1
    IF DataArray[Position] > Value THEN
        WHILE Position >= 1 AND DataArray[Position] > Value
            DataArray[Position + 1] <- DataArray[Position]
            Position <- Position - 1
        ENDWHILE
        DataArray[Position + 1] <- Value
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
items.notes: Lower-case 'to' in the mark scheme corrected to TO; en dashes replaced with hyphens.

items.term: Copy a text file (OPENFILE / READFILE / WRITEFILE)
items.prompt: Copy all the lines from FileA.txt to FileB.txt, replacing any blank lines by a line of dashes.
items.answer:
DECLARE LineOfText : STRING
OPENFILE "FileA.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "FileB.txt" FOR WRITE
WHILE NOT EOF("FileA.txt")
    READFILE "FileA.txt", LineOfText
    IF LineOfText = "" THEN
        WRITEFILE "FileB.txt", " ----------------------------"
    ELSE
        WRITEFILE "FileB.txt", LineOfText
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE "FileA.txt"
CLOSEFILE "FileB.txt"
items.notes: Files are opened in one mode at a time (READ, WRITE or APPEND), tested with EOF and closed with CLOSEFILE.

items.prompt: StudentFile.Dat is a random file of Student records. Move the records in positions 10 to 20 up one place, then store NewPupil in position 10.
items.answer:
OPENFILE "StudentFile.Dat" FOR RANDOM
FOR Position <- 20 TO 10 STEP -1
    SEEK "StudentFile.Dat", Position
    GETRECORD "StudentFile.Dat", Pupil
    SEEK "StudentFile.Dat", Position + 1
    PUTRECORD "StudentFile.Dat", Pupil
NEXT Position
SEEK "StudentFile.Dat", 10
PUTRECORD "StudentFile.Dat", NewPupil
CLOSEFILE "StudentFile.Dat"
items.notes: Trimmed from the guide's example (the DECLAREs and the NewPupil assignments are omitted). The guide's last line has a lower-case file name (.dat); made consistent with the OPENFILE line.

items.term: Check a file has enough lines (function)
items.prompt: Write a function CheckFile(ThisFile) that returns TRUE if the text file contains more than 9 non-blank lines, otherwise FALSE. Stop reading as soon as the answer is known.
items.answer:
FUNCTION CheckFile(ThisFile : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    DECLARE Valid : BOOLEAN
    DECLARE ThisLine : STRING
    DECLARE Count : INTEGER
    Count <- 0
    Valid <- FALSE
    OPENFILE ThisFile FOR READ
    WHILE NOT EOF(ThisFile) AND Valid = FALSE
        READFILE ThisFile, ThisLine
        IF ThisLine <> "" THEN
            Count <- Count + 1
            IF Count > 9 THEN
                Valid <- TRUE
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    CLOSEFILE ThisFile
    RETURN Valid
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The mark scheme writes 'OPEN ThisFile FOR READ'; the keyword is OPENFILE. The parameter name Thisfile in the heading was made ThisFile to match the body.

items.prompt: Write a procedure CreateFiles(NameRoot, NumFiles) that creates NumFiles text files named NameRoot.001, NameRoot.002 and so on, each containing the single line 'This is File <file name>'.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE CreateFiles(NameRoot : STRING, NumFiles : INTEGER)
    DECLARE FileName, Suffix : STRING
    DECLARE Count : INTEGER
    FOR Count <- 1 TO NumFiles
        Suffix <- NUM_TO_STR(Count)
        WHILE LENGTH(Suffix) <> 3
            Suffix <- '0' & Suffix
        ENDWHILE
        FileName <- NameRoot & '.' & Suffix
        OPENFILE FileName FOR WRITE
        WRITEFILE FileName, "This is File " & FileName
        CLOSEFILE FileName
    NEXT Count
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: The suffix is padded to three digits with a WHILE loop. The mark scheme heading wraps over two lines.

items.prompt: Write a function Stage_1(StudentName) that copies StudentName_src.txt to StudentName_S1.txt, removing comments from each line with DeleteComment() and not writing lines that become empty. Return the number of lines written.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Stage_1(StudentName : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE OldFile, NewFile, Line : STRING
    DECLARE Count : INTEGER
    OldFile <- StudentName & "_src.txt"
    NewFile <- StudentName & "_S1.txt"
    OPENFILE OldFile FOR READ
    OPENFILE NewFile FOR WRITE
    Count <- 0
    WHILE NOT EOF(OldFile)
        READFILE OldFile, Line
        Line <- DeleteComment(Line)
        IF LENGTH(Line) <> 0 THEN
            WRITEFILE NewFile, Line
            Count <- Count + 1
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    CLOSEFILE OldFile
    CLOSEFILE NewFile
    RETURN Count
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: File names are built by concatenation and held in variables, so the variables are used as file identifiers.

items.term: Read a file and count by group (control break)
items.prompt: TimeTaken.txt holds one record per line, in time order, each starting with a two-digit hour. Write pseudocode that outputs each hour and how many lines have that hour.
items.answer:
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
DECLARE Line : STRING
DECLARE NextHour, Hour : STRING
OPENFILE "TimeTaken.txt" FOR READ
Count <- 1
READFILE "TimeTaken.txt", Line
Hour <- LEFT(Line, 2)
WHILE NOT EOF("TimeTaken.txt")
    READFILE "TimeTaken.txt", Line
    NextHour <- LEFT(Line, 2)
    IF NextHour = Hour THEN
        Count <- Count + 1
    ELSE
        OUTPUT "Hour : ", Hour, " Total : ", Count
        Hour <- NextHour
        Count <- 1
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT "Hour : ", Hour, " Total : ", Count
CLOSEFILE "TimeTaken.txt"
items.notes: First of two example solutions. The first line is read before the loop and the last group is output after the loop.

items.term: Write array records to a text file
items.prompt: Character is an array of 45 records (fields Player, Role, Name and Level). Write a procedure Save() that writes each record to SaveFile.txt as one line, with the fields separated by '^'.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE Save()
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    DECLARE Line : STRING
    CONSTANT SEP = '^'
    OPENFILE "SaveFile.txt" FOR WRITE
    FOR Index <- 1 TO 45
        Line <- NUM_TO_STR(Character[Index].Player) & SEP
        Line <- Line & Character[Index].Role & SEP
        Line <- Line & Character[Index].Name & SEP
        Line <- Line & NUM_TO_STR(Character[Index].Level)
        WRITEFILE "SaveFile.txt", Line
    NEXT Index
    CLOSEFILE "SaveFile.txt"
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Numeric fields are converted with NUM_TO_STR before concatenation. Spacing in the DECLARE lines tidied.

items.term: Random file: read a chosen record in a loop
items.prompt: StockList.dat is a random file of 500 STRING records. Write pseudocode that repeatedly asks for a location from 1 to 500, outputs the item stored there (or that the record is missing), and asks whether to continue.
items.answer:
DECLARE Location : INTEGER
DECLARE Item : STRING
DECLARE Continue : BOOLEAN
DECLARE Answer : CHAR
Continue <- TRUE
OPENFILE "StockList.dat" FOR RANDOM
WHILE Continue
    OUTPUT "Enter a location between 1 and 500: "
    INPUT Location
    SEEK "StockList.dat", Location

OUTPUT "End of program"

items.prompt: Declare a stack of up to 40 REAL values held in an array Stack with BasePointer and TopPointer, and write a procedure Initialise() that makes the stack empty.
items.answer:
CONSTANT MaxSize = 40
DECLARE BasePointer : INTEGER
DECLARE TopPointer : INTEGER
DECLARE Stack : ARRAY[1:40] OF REAL
PROCEDURE Initialise()
    BasePointer <- 1
    TopPointer <- 0
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: An empty stack has TopPointer one below BasePointer. Comments dropped.

items.prompt: Write a procedure Push(NewItem) that adds a REAL value to the stack (array Stack, pointers BasePointer and TopPointer, constant MaxSize) if there is room.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE Push(NewItem : REAL)
    IF TopPointer < MaxSize THEN
        TopPointer <- TopPointer + 1
        Stack[TopPointer] <- NewItem
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: The mark scheme heading omits the parameter type (Push(NewItem)); ': REAL' added to match the stack's element type.

items.prompt: The stack is an array Stack[1:25] of REAL with BasePointer and TopPointer. Write a function Pop() that returns the top value, or outputs an error message and returns 0 if the stack is empty.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Pop() RETURNS REAL
    DECLARE Item : REAL
    Item <- 0
    IF TopPointer >= BasePointer THEN
        Item <- Stack[TopPointer]
        TopPointer <- TopPointer - 1
    ELSE
        OUTPUT "The stack is empty - error"
    ENDIF
    RETURN Item
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: En dashes replaced with hyphens; the leading // comment dropped.

items.prompt: ThisStack is an array of 60 REAL values with stack pointer SP (next free position) and OnStack (count of items). Write a function Push(ThisValue) that returns FALSE if the stack is full, otherwise stores the value and returns TRUE.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Push(ThisValue : REAL) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    DECLARE ReturnValue : BOOLEAN
    IF OnStack = 60 THEN
        RETURN FALSE
    ENDIF
    ThisStack[SP] <- ThisValue
    SP <- SP + 1
    OnStack <- OnStack + 1
    RETURN TRUE
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The mark scheme lists several accepted full-stack tests (OnStack = 60, SP > 60, etc.); the first is used. The unused DECLARE ReturnValue is as in the example solution. The // comment was dropped.

items.prompt: The print queue is a circular array Queue[1:60] with FrontPointer, RearPointer, Length and MaxSize. Write a function Dequeue() that returns the item at the front, resetting the queue with CALL Initialise when it becomes empty, wrapping FrontPointer round, and returning "" with an error message when the queue is empty.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Dequeue() RETURNS STRING
    DECLARE Item : STRING
    IF Length > 0 THEN
        Item <- Queue[FrontPointer]
        FrontPointer <- FrontPointer + 1
        Length <- Length - 1
        IF Length = 0 THEN
            CALL Initialise
        ELSE
            IF FrontPointer > MaxSize THEN
                FrontPointer <- 1
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ELSE
        OUTPUT "The print queue was empty - error"
        Item <- ""
    ENDIF
    RETURN Item
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The mark scheme writes 'FUNCTION Dequeue RETURNS STRING' without brackets; () added to follow the guide. En dashes replaced with hyphens; // comment dropped.

items.prompt: Declare a circular queue of STRING of up to 50 items (array Queue indexed from 0, FrontPointer, RearPointer, Length) and write a procedure Initialise() that makes it empty.
items.answer:
CONSTANT MaxLength = 50
DECLARE FrontPointer : INTEGER
DECLARE RearPointer : INTEGER
DECLARE Length : INTEGER
DECLARE Queue : ARRAY[0:MaxLength - 1] OF STRING
PROCEDURE Initialise()
    FrontPointer <- -1
    RearPointer <- -1
    Length <- 0
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: Comments dropped; en dash replaced with a hyphen. Brackets added to the procedure name (the mark scheme writes PROCEDURE Initialise).

items.prompt: Write a procedure Enqueue(NewItem) for the circular queue Queue[0:MaxLength - 1] (pointers FrontPointer, RearPointer, Length) that adds the item if the queue is not full, wrapping RearPointer back to 0 when it passes the end of the array.
items.answer:
PROCEDURE Enqueue(NewItem : STRING)
    IF Length < MaxLength THEN
        RearPointer <- RearPointer + 1
        IF RearPointer > MaxLength - 1 THEN
            RearPointer <- 0
        ENDIF
        Queue[RearPointer] <- NewItem
        Length <- Length + 1
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
items.notes: The mark scheme also accepts Length <= MaxLength - 1 as the full test. Comments dropped.

items.prompt: A queue is held in a record AQueue with an array QueueArray[0:99] and pointers HeadPointer and TailPointer (HeadPointer is -1 when empty). Write a function Enqueue(AQueue, TheData) that returns 1 if the item is added and -1 if the queue is full.
items.answer:
FUNCTION Enqueue(BYREF AQueue : Queue, BYVAL TheData : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF AQueue.HeadPointer = -1 THEN
        AQueue.QueueArray[AQueue.TailPointer] <- TheData
        AQueue.HeadPointer <- 0
        AQueue.TailPointer <- AQueue.TailPointer + 1
        RETURN 1
    ELSE
        IF AQueue.TailPointer > 99 THEN
            RETURN -1
        ELSE
            AQueue.QueueArray[AQueue.TailPointer] <- TheData
            AQueue.TailPointer <- AQueue.TailPointer + 1
            RETURN 1
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Paper 4 model answer given as pseudocode. The record is passed by reference because it is modified. The heading wraps in the mark scheme.

items.prompt: A linked list is held in arrays Flower and NextPointer, starting at HeadPointer, with 0 as the null pointer. Write pseudocode that inputs a flower name, searches the list and outputs whether it was found.

items.prompt: A binary tree is stored in the array BinTree of records with Data, LeftPtr and RightPtr; RootPtr points to the root and -1 is the null pointer. Write a function SearchTree(Item) that returns the position of Item, or -1 if it is not in the tree.
items.answer:
FUNCTION SearchTree(Item : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER
    NowPtr <- RootPtr
    WHILE NowPtr <> -1
        IF BinTree[NowPtr].Data > Item THEN
            NowPtr <- BinTree[NowPtr].LeftPtr
        ELSE
            IF BinTree[NowPtr].Data < Item THEN
                NowPtr <- BinTree[NowPtr].RightPtr
            ELSE
                RETURN NowPtr
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN NowPtr
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Go left when the stored item is greater than the search item, right when it is smaller; when NowPtr reaches -1 the item is not present and -1 is returned.

items.prompt: A binary tree is stored in the 2D array ArrayNodes: column 0 is the left pointer, column 1 the data and column 2 the right pointer, with -1 meaning no node. Write a recursive function SearchValue(Root, ValueToFind) that returns the index of the node holding the value, or -1.
items.answer:
FUNCTION SearchValue(BYVAL Root : INTEGER, ValueToFind : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Root = -1 THEN
        RETURN -1
    ELSE
        IF ArrayNodes[Root, 1] = ValueToFind THEN
            RETURN Root
        ELSE
            IF ArrayNodes[Root, 1] = -1 THEN
                RETURN -1
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    IF ArrayNodes[Root, 1] > ValueToFind THEN
        RETURN SearchValue(ArrayNodes[Root, 0], ValueToFind)
    ENDIF
    IF ArrayNodes[Root, 1] < ValueToFind THEN
        RETURN SearchValue(ArrayNodes[Root, 2], ValueToFind)
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Paper 4 model answer. The mark scheme heading has no RETURNS clause; ' RETURNS INTEGER' added and the heading joined onto one line.

items.prompt: Write a recursive function RecursiveValue(Number, ToFind) that returns the sum of all the whole numbers from 1 to Number that divide exactly into ToFind.
items.answer:
FUNCTION RecursiveValue(Number : INTEGER, ToFind : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Number = 0 THEN
        RETURN 0
    ELSE
        IF ToFind MOD Number = 0 THEN
            RETURN Number + RecursiveValue(Number - 1, ToFind)
        ELSE
            RETURN RecursiveValue(Number - 1, ToFind)
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Paper 4 model answer. The mark scheme writes the operator as MODULUS and the type as Integer; MOD and INTEGER used here. Base case Number = 0, then a recursive call on Number - 1 in each branch.

items.prompt: Write a function CheckInfo(NewLine) that returns TRUE only if NewLine has at least 19 characters, its first four characters are all numeric and between "0001" and "5999", and characters 5 to 7 are alphabetic (use OnlyAlpha()).
items.answer:
FUNCTION CheckInfo(NewLine : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    DECLARE ThisNum : STRING
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    IF LENGTH(NewLine) < 19 THEN
        RETURN FALSE
    ENDIF
    FOR Index <- 1 TO 4
        IF NOT IS_NUM(MID(NewLine, Index, 1)) THEN
            RETURN FALSE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
    ThisNum <- LEFT(NewLine, 4)
    IF ThisNum < "0001" OR ThisNum > "5999" THEN
        RETURN FALSE
    ENDIF
    IF NOT OnlyAlpha(MID(NewLine, 5, 3)) THEN
        RETURN FALSE
    ENDIF
    RETURN TRUE
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: The mark scheme spells the parameter Newline in the body; NewLine used throughout. Marks: length test, extract first four characters, numeric test, range test, extract characters 5 to 7, OnlyAlpha(), RETURN a BOOLEAN in every case.

items.term: Add an entry to sorted parallel arrays (function)
items.prompt: ErrCode[1:500] and ErrText[1:500] hold error numbers and messages, with unused entries holding 999. Write a function AddError(ErrNum, ErrMess) that stores a new error in the first unused entry, calls SortArrays(), and returns the number of unused entries remaining, or -1 if there was no room.
items.answer:
FUNCTION AddError(ErrNum : INTEGER, ErrMess : STRING) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Index, Remaining : INTEGER
    CONSTANT Unused = 999
    Index <- 1
    Remaining <- -1
    REPEAT
        IF ErrCode[Index] = Unused THEN
            ErrCode[Index] <- ErrNum
            ErrText[Index] <- ErrMess
            CALL SortArrays()
            Remaining <- 500 - Index
        ENDIF
        Index <- Index + 1
    UNTIL Remaining <> -1 OR Index > 500
    RETURN Remaining
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Heading wraps over two lines in the mark scheme. En dash replaced with a hyphen.

items.prompt: Membership is an array of 3000 Student records with fields StudentID, Club_1, Club_2 and Club_3. Write a procedure GetIDs() that inputs a club number, outputs the StudentID of every student in that club, and then outputs how many students are in the club.

PROCEDURE GetIDs()
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER

    Count <- 0
    FOR Index <- 1 TO 3000
        IF Membership[Index].Club_1 = ThisClub OR Membership[Index].Club_2 = ThisClub OR Membership[Index].Club_3 = ThisClub THEN

items.term: Store a new record in the first free slot (function)
items.prompt: Loan is an array of 7000 records with fields StudentID, BookID and OnLoan; an unused entry has a blank StudentID. Write a function NewLoan(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID) that stores a new loan in the first unused entry and returns TRUE, or returns FALSE if there is no room.
items.answer:
FUNCTION NewLoan(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    DECLARE IsStored : BOOLEAN
    CONSTANT Blank = ""
    Index <- 1
    IsStored <- FALSE
    WHILE Index <= 7000 AND NOT IsStored
        IF Loan[Index].StudentID = Blank THEN
            Loan[Index].StudentID <- ThisStudentID
            Loan[Index].BookID <- ThisBookID
            Loan[Index].OnLoan <- TRUE
            IsStored <- TRUE
        ENDIF
        Index <- Index + 1
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN IsStored
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: First example solution. The heading wraps over three lines in the mark scheme (continuation marker __).

items.term: Find a matching record and update it (function)
items.prompt: Loan is an array of 5000 records with fields StudentID, BookID and OnLoan. Write a function ReturnBook(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID) that marks the matching loan as returned and returns TRUE, or returns FALSE if no matching loan exists or it was already returned.
items.answer:
FUNCTION ReturnBook(ThisStudentID, ThisBookID : STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    DECLARE Index : INTEGER
    Index <- 1
    WHILE Index < 5001
        IF Loan[Index].StudentID = ThisStudentID AND Loan[Index].BookID = ThisBookID THEN
            IF Loan[Index].OnLoan = TRUE THEN
                Loan[Index].OnLoan <- FALSE
                RETURN TRUE
            ELSE
                RETURN FALSE
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
        Index <- Index + 1
    ENDWHILE
    RETURN FALSE
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: First example solution. 'False' capitalised to FALSE; short // comments dropped; the condition joined onto one line (the mark scheme uses the continuation marker __).

items.prompt: Write a function GetField(Msg, FieldNo) that returns characters 2 to 4 of Msg for field 1, characters 5 to 7 for field 2, and for field 3 the text from character 8 up to but not including the last character; any other field number returns an empty string.
items.answer:
FUNCTION GetField(Msg : STRING, FieldNo : INTEGER) RETURNS STRING
    DECLARE RetString : STRING
    CASE OF FieldNo
        1 : RetString <- MID(Msg, 2, 3)
        2 : RetString <- MID(Msg, 5, 3)
        3 : RetString <- MID(Msg, 8, LENGTH(Msg) - 8)
        OTHERWISE : RetString <- ""
    ENDCASE
    RETURN RetString
ENDFUNCTION
items.notes: Heading wraps over two lines in the mark scheme. Each CASE branch is a single statement here.
